5) On-prem / private deployment options and timeline if we require an in-region private deployment for regulated data.

Marissa / Karthik / Sara — adding a technical supplement that we can include in the evidence pack. This is intended for the technical reviewers.

1) Transfer mechanism & DPA language: 
- Default: EU SCCs (European Commission 2021 clauses) embedded into our DPA annex. 
- Alternative: For customers requiring DPF coverage, Redwood can provide attestation and contractual language referencing reliance on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework where applicable; we require an annex execution and operational questionnaire for DPF reliance.
- Example DPA snippet (for your legal team): "Redwood commits not to use Customer Data to train models or improve model parameters; processing for model improvement, if any, is performed only on aggregated telemetry that does not include Customer Data as defined in Section 2." (We will provide final legal-approved text from Karthik.)

2) Technical controls (short):
- In transit: TLS 1.3 preferred, fallback to 1.2; mTLS available for Dedicated/Private connectors.
- At rest: AES-256-GCM. Data volumes and key material separated per-tenant.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS.
- KV cache: we keep the inference KV cache ephemeral by default; configurable TTL and explicit cache-clearing APIs. Cache is namespaced per-tenant, and subprocessors cannot access KV cache outside the Redwood runtime.
- Pseudonymization: we support tokenization hooks in the request pipeline and a prompt-scrubbing preprocessor; recommended for PHI.
- Model routing & residency: requests are routed to region-bound pools by policy (latency/residency); fallback to compatible variants in the same legal jurisdiction unless customer allows cross-jurisdiction fallback.

3) Observability & export: 
- Audit logs: API call logs, model/route used, token counts, and response hash are retained and exportable. Default retention 90 days (EU-bearing region), configurable to 730 days under Enterprise plan. Exports available as Parquet via secure S3 or secure Drive link.

4) Subprocessors & escrow: 
- Active subprocessors list attached. We require subprocessors to sign contractual commitments aligned to our DPA and to operate under the same transfer mechanisms. 
- Escrow/assurance: for high-regulation customers we offer a subprocessor escrow snapshot as part of onboarding and quarterly attestations.

5) On-prem: 
- Private deployment: VPC control plane + in-region inference pool. Typical timeline 4–6 weeks for Dedicated; on-prem air-gapped option can be 8–12 weeks depending on site readiness.

I'll attach a short technical annex (redwood-crossborder-evidence-20260615.pdf) with diagrams and key evidence artifacts (SCCs excerpt, key separation design, sample audit export).

-David
David Kim
Privacy & Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sara — appreciate the quick turnaround on your sheet. Consolidated response below and attached final artifacts.

A) Legal commitments (redline-ready):
- Non-training clause (Karthik): "Provider (Redwood Inference) shall not use Customer Personal Data to train, fine-tune, or improve underlying model parameters or weights. Provider may only process aggregated telemetry that is irreversibly aggregated and does not contain Customer Personal Data for service health and capacity planning." (Attached: sccs-execution-draft.docx — contains this clause in the DPA annex template under section 7.2). 
- SCCs approach: Redwood is neutral; our standard is to append the SCCs as an annex to the DPA (we provide an executed addendum on request). We'll append for ClinicalBridge as requested.

B) Cache & subprocessors (David):
- Tenant isolation: KV cache is namespaced per-tenant and stored in region-local ephemeral stores. Default TTL is ephemeral per-request, configurable by policy (we do not persist KV cache to long-term storage in hosted mode). For Dedicated/Private, customers can opt to host caches in their VPC or to enable explicit cache-purge on session end. Subprocessors cannot access KV cache outside the runtime.
- Formal statement (for RFP cell): "Redwood confirms KV cache is tenant-isolated, not exported to subprocessors, and not used to train or improve models." (See redwood-crossborder-evidence-20260615.pdf for architecture diagram and cache lifecycle).

C) Logs & retention: default 90 days in-region, exportable. Enterprise export to secure S3/Parquet available up to 730 days. Audit exports include request metadata but do not contain raw output content unless customer enables full transcript export.

D) KMS & encryption: AES-256-GCM at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit. Customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers may choose HSM-backed Redwood KMS.

E) On-prem/private timeline: Private VPC: 4–6 weeks; Air-gapped on-prem package: 8–12 weeks (subject to network access & security review).

F) Attachments & evidence: attached to this thread — redwood-crossborder-evidence-20260615.pdf (technical annex, diagrams, export samples), sccs-execution-draft.docx (DPA annex + SCCs appendix), subprocessor-declaration-20260615.csv (live subprocessors list).

Next steps: 
1) We will append the non-training clause and SCCs to the DPA and share a redline by EOD Friday. (Karthik taking point).
2) If helpful, let's run a 30-minute technical call Monday 2026-06-21 09:30–10:00 CET. Confirm and we'll send calendar invite.

Thanks — happy to escalate to an on-site proof-of-concept for audit if that's required for procurement.
